title: US Care Safety Signals: federal data analyses of caregiver injury and patient harm during patient handling and transfer
description:
Analyses of public US federal data on injuries to caregivers and harm to patients during patient handling and transfer in hospitals and nursing facilities.

Contents. Thirteen analyses covering: resident-handling injuries (5,654 of 25,860 nursing-facility cases reported to OSHA for 2025); the handling task under way, including about 1,440 hospital injuries during lateral transfers between surfaces; lifting equipment mentioned in injury narratives; injury rates per 100 full-time workers, with a facility-level dataset of 7,554 establishments; three-year trends for 2023-2025; workers' compensation and indirect cost estimates; violence against caregivers; patient harm across 14,439 FDA MAUDE reports for patient lifts, transfer devices and stretchers (2015-2025); hospital-acquired pressure injury and HACRP penalty status across 3,056 hospitals; graded record linkages connecting 8,047 OSHA establishments to CMS-certified nursing homes and 3,180 to CMS hospitals; an out-of-sample validation of the classification rules against OSHA's own OIICS coding on 28,074 cases; and a pre-specified protocol for evaluating a change in how patients are moved.

Method. Every text-classification rule is frozen, then validated against blind human review and against OSHA's professional injury coding on data the rules were not built on. Measured precision is reported and applied to published counts. Negative results, a pre-registered analysis plan, and two publicly corrected errors are included.

Privacy and disclosure. Facilities are identified by federal identifier (CCN or OSHA establishment ID) and state only; no facility name appears. No product is evaluated, recommended, or compared. The case narratives are employer-written text published by OSHA and are reproduced verbatim so the review samples can be audited against the source; a few of them name a product, in the employers' words. The author's commercial interest is disclosed in the repository README.

Sources. OSHA Injury Tracking Application (case detail and Form 300A summary), FDA MAUDE via openFDA, and CMS Provider Data Catalog.
